answer: Your records do not list any allergies or drug intolerances. The allergy section of your record is empty. That does not fully rule out an allergy, because allergies are often recorded only when someone asks about them or when a reaction happens. If you know of a reaction to a medicine, food, or other substance, tell your doctor and pharmacist so it can be added to your record, and check before starting any new medicine.
short: No allergies or drug intolerances are recorded in her pod. The record may be incomplete, so the patient should confirm with her doctor and pharmacist.

items.says: No allergies or drug intolerances are recorded in your records.
items.why: The allergy list in your record is empty, and no allergy or intolerance appears in any other part of the records I can see.

absences.what: Any allergy or drug intolerance recorded in the pod.
absences.coverage: The full pod read (active allergies view, condition history, medication history, active medications, procedures, lab results, reports and documents, the person record), all three sources (S1, S2, S3).

knowledge.says: An empty allergy list often means no allergy was ever recorded, not that a person is certain to have none; reactions that were never written down can still be real and matter for prescribing.
